newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Air NZ signs pact with United.
newsitem.headline: Air NZ signs pact with United.

text.p: Air New Zealand Ltd, half owner of Ansett Australia, said on Tuesday it had signed a commercial alliance with United Airlines.

Under the alliance agreement, the two airlines will continue to operate current levels of aircraft capacity on routes which they both fly within the Pacific region, and will develop arrangements to share their carrying capacity and other infrastructure, Air New Zealand said.

The arrangement would significantly increase the number of trans-Pacific flights that each airline can offer its customers, and the number of city-to-city connections that the two airlines can provide between the United States and New Zealand or Australia.
Air NZ said the pact with United, the world's largest airline, created a strong foundation to develop other partnerships to cover areas where Air NZ had nil or limited coverage.
Previously, the company has said it was looking for alliances with a European or Asian airline or both.
The United deal will be introduced progressively from March.
United has access to 251 destinations in the United States.
Air NZ said the economies of both Australia and New Zealand stood to make significant gains from the deal.

"It marks a real breakthrough in terms of our ability to develop the vital North American tourism market, and to extend and improve the services we can offer Australia and New Zealand travellers to the United States and beyond," Air NZ Managing Director Jim McCrea said.
The deal would streamline check-in procedures and include mutual recognition of frequent flyer schemes.
